points.description: Parity invariant: both x+2 and 3x preserve the parity of a number, so a and b must have the same parity. Pairs of opposite parity can never be equal.

Mod 4 invariant for odd numbers: for odd x, both x+2 and 3x change the residue mod 4 (1↔3), so if a, b are both odd, they flip together each step and stay congruent/incongruent mod 4 forever. Hence odd pairs with a≢b (mod 4) are impossible. Even pairs must NOT be excluded by a mod 4 argument (even numbers can change relative residue mod 4 since 3x keeps 0 and 2 fixed while +2 swaps them).

points.description: Sufficiency for odd a≡b (mod 4), a≠b: gives a valid argument or construction (any correct method, e.g. reducing the difference using mixed operations) showing the numbers can be made equal. Mere assertion or checking a few examples earns no more than the part-mark.

points.description: Sufficiency for both even (distinct): gives a valid argument or construction showing any two distinct even numbers can be made equal (e.g. via halving to ops m→m+1, m→3m, or direct explicit sequences; example (2,4): 2→3·2=6, 4→4+2=6). Mere assertion or a few examples earns no more than the part-mark.

levels.says: Verifies only specific examples or gives an incomplete construction that does not cover all even pairs.

points.description: Final answer: all pairs with both even, or both odd with a≡b (mod 4). (Equivalently: a≡b mod 2, excluding odd pairs with a≡b+2 mod 4.)

rubric.notes: Full marks need the necessity arguments (parity, mod 4 for odd) and valid sufficiency arguments for both families, plus the correct final answer. Award part marks for invariants proved correctly even if sufficiency is only checked on examples. A wrong final family (e.g. requiring a≡b mod 4 for all pairs, or excluding even pairs) loses P4/P5 but keeps credit for correct earlier steps.
rubric.answer_key: Parity is preserved by both operations, so a≡b (mod 2) is necessary. For odd x, x+2 and 3x each switch the residue mod 4 between 1 and 3, so two odd numbers switch together each step and a≡b (mod 4) is necessary for odd pairs. For even numbers, writing x=2m turns the operations into m→m+1 and m→3m. Any two distinct even numbers can then be made equal (e.g. (2,4): 2→6 by ×3, 4→6 by +2). Odd pairs with a≡b (mod 4) can also be made equal by a similar construction. Answer: all pairs (a,b) with both even, or both odd with a≡b (mod 4).
